summary: All three round-1 code-review findings (M1, m1, m2) are correctly addressed across b84a031 and b092178. The subsequent SA2-driven commit 719b5c8 adds correct security hardening: raw env-var string removed from INFO/DEBUG logs, and a char-boundary-safe bound_log_value helper bounds the parse-failure WARN to 16 chars. All changes verified correct with no new issues.

M1_code_review.description: seed_jwt_ttl_from_env uses get_or_init with a captured Option<u64>. INFO fires only when newly_seeded_value is Some (this call won the init race). Re-seed path emits DEBUG with the already-stored value. Log truthfulness verified: stored comes from *JWT_TTL.get_or_init(...) which returns the actual lock value regardless of which call populated it.
M1_code_review.note_on_719b5c8: SA2-R1-M1 further strips the raw env-var string from both INFO and DEBUG — only the resolved numeric TTL is logged. Correct tightening: operator who pastes MCP_JWT_SECRET into MCP_JWT_TTL_SECS no longer leaks it through log aggregation.

m1_whitespace_assertion.description: Second logs_contain assertion placed after the whitespace-only call, independently verifying the WARN fires for Some('   '). TR2-R1-1 attribution comment present.

m2_visibility.description: JWT_TTL_DEFAULT_SECS, JWT_TTL_MIN_SECS, JWT_TTL_MAX_SECS are now pub(crate). No external files reference these constants.

changes_reviewed: INFO log: raw MCP_JWT_TTL_SECS string removed; only resolved numeric TTL logged.
DEBUG log: same — raw string removed; only already-stored numeric TTL logged.
New private fn bound_log_value(s: &str, max_chars: usize) -> String — char-boundary-safe truncation via chars().take(max_chars) + ellipsis on overflow.
compute_jwt_ttl_from_env_str parse-failure WARN: trimmed echoed through bound_log_value(trimmed, 16).
New test jwt_ttl_parse_failure_warn_bounds_raw_value: 17-char input, asserts first 16 present + ellipsis + 17th absent.
New test bound_log_value_truncates_to_max_chars: no-truncation, exact-length, over-length, empty, multi-byte UTF-8.

correctness_notes.bound_log_value_impl: CORRECT — chars().take(max_chars) is char-boundary-safe. iter.next() after the take detects overflow without advancing past a char boundary. collect() handles multi-byte chars correctly.
correctness_notes.utf8_test_case: CORRECT — 'üü🦀abc' with max_chars=3: takes ü, ü, 🦀 (3 chars); iter.next() = Some('a'); result = 'üü🦀…'. Assertion matches.
correctness_notes.existing_test_compat: CORRECT — 'notanumber' is 10 chars (< 16 limit); bound_log_value returns it unchanged. Existing logs_contain assertion for that string still passes.
correctness_notes.visibility: bound_log_value is module-private (fn, not pub fn) — correct for an internal logging utility.
correctness_notes.test_attrs: jwt_ttl_parse_failure_warn_bounds_raw_value uses #[tracing_test::traced_test] + #[test] correctly. bound_log_value_truncates_to_max_chars uses only #[test] — correct, no tracing involved.

positive_observations: get_or_init is the idiomatic OnceLock API for this pattern — eliminates the misleading log from round 1.
Removing the raw env-var from logs proactively closes a potential credential-leakage path that the spec's Decision-14 logging policy is designed to prevent.
bound_log_value uses chars() not byte slices — correct char-boundary-safe approach for UTF-8 attacker input.
The 16-char bound is well-chosen: 'notanumber' (10 chars) fits without truncation so existing test assertions remain valid, while a 1 MB attacker payload is cut to a fixed short prefix.
overall_assessment: All round-1 findings resolved. 719b5c8 security hardening is correct, well-tested, and introduces no regressions. Round 2 verdict: APPROVE.
